label: European Countries Under France's Extended Nuclear Deterrence
value: 9 Nations (UK, DE, PL, NL, SE, DK, BE, GR, NO)
source: SCMP May 28, 2026; UNITED24 Media May 28, 2026; Narvik Agreement signing, Paris
contestNote: Norway became the 9th European country to enter France's nuclear umbrella framework via the Narvik Agreement (May 28). The French nuclear guarantee is bilateral and not integrated into NATO's Nuclear Planning Group (NPG) — it supplements rather than replaces US extended deterrence. France's force de frappe (approximately 300 warheads, SNLE submarines + ASMP-A air-launched missiles) anchors the framework. The expansion is explicitly driven by US signals of zero submarine contribution to NATO and uncertainty over NATO NPG commitments under Trump. The bilateral format means the guarantee is not subject to Article 5 conditionality debates.
deltaNote: France began offering 'strategic dialogue' on extended deterrence in 2024. The Narvik Agreement (May 28, 2026) is the most consequential expansion to date — Norway's Arctic border with Russia and its High North surveillance infrastructure makes it strategically the most significant addition to the French nuclear guarantee network.
